intro: Most homeowners in Bonnyrigg start thinking seriously about underfloor heating when they're already halfway through a renovation — they've got the floors up, the heating system is being updated, and someone mentions it's the perfect time. They're right. Underfloor heating is one of those upgrades that genuinely transforms how a home feels day to day, eliminating cold spots, freeing up wall space from radiators, and running more efficiently than traditional systems. Whether you're updating a period cottage near the town centre or finishing a new build on one of Bonnyrigg's modern estates, getting this installed properly from the outset saves a huge amount of hassle and expense later.
localContext: Bonnyrigg has a genuinely mixed housing stock, and that matters a lot when you're planning underfloor heating. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the town present real challenges — solid stone floors, limited insulation beneath existing floorboards, and older boilers that weren't designed to run the lower flow temperatures that underfloor heating prefers. Getting these right requires an installer who understands the specific demands of older construction, not just someone who fits systems in new builds. On Bonnyrigg's more modern estates, wet underfloor heating is often straightforward to integrate, especially during a new build or major refurbishment. It's also worth noting that Bonnyrigg sits in a moderately hard water area, which means a proper inhibitor and system filter should always be fitted as part of any wet underfloor heating installation — limescale build-up in manifolds and pipework is a real issue if this step is skipped, and it quietly reduces efficiency and lifespan over time.
serviceDetail: A wet underfloor heating installation in Bonnyrigg typically follows a clear sequence, though the specifics vary depending on whether you're retrofitting into an older stone property or building from scratch on a new development. The process begins with a heat loss calculation for each room — this determines the pipe spacing and flow rates needed to actually heat the space, rather than just warming the floor slightly. An experienced installer will also assess whether your existing boiler can handle the system or whether an upgrade to a heat pump or new condensing boiler is advisable. Next comes the groundwork: insulation boards are laid first, which is non-negotiable if you want the heat going upward into the room rather than downward into the ground. The pipework is then clipped or stapled to the insulation in a carefully planned pattern, connected back to a manifold, and pressure tested before anything goes on top. A screed or specialist overlay is poured or laid over the pipework, and you'll typically need to wait several weeks for it to cure before finishing floors can go down. The system is then commissioned, flow rates balanced across zones, and the thermostat controls set up room by room. For Bonnyrigg's older properties, this process often includes additional prep work to address uneven subfloors or inadequate existing insulation, which adds time but is essential for the system to perform properly.
pricing: In Bonnyrigg, a wet underfloor heating installation typically costs between £3,000 and £8,000, depending on the size of the project and the complexity involved. A single room retrofit in an older stone-built property, where floor build-up needs careful management and existing joists may need work, sits at the lower end. A whole-ground-floor installation across a larger modern estate home, complete with multi-zone manifold, programmable controls, and screed, will reach the higher end. Additional costs to factor in include boiler upgrades if your existing system isn't compatible, floor preparation work in period cottages, and the finishing floor material — some choices like thick solid wood or deep carpet significantly reduce efficiency and aren't recommended.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Bonnyrigg well makes a genuine difference on a job like this. Someone familiar with the town's housing stock understands the quirks of older stone-built properties — the uneven floors, the lack of sub-floor insulation, the older pipework that might need upgrading at the same time. They're also likely to have working relationships with local suppliers and be easier to contact if a question comes up after the job is done. Underfloor heating is a long-term investment, and having an installer who'll still be local and contactable when you need a manifold adjusted or a zone checked in three years' time is genuinely valuable.

faqs.q: Is underfloor heating practical in Bonnyrigg's older stone-built homes?
faqs.a: Yes, but it requires more planning than a modern property. The main challenges are floor build-up height, sub-floor insulation, and ensuring the existing boiler can run at lower flow temperatures. A good installer will assess all of this upfront. Retrofit systems using lower-profile insulation boards are well suited to Bonnyrigg's period cottages where floor height is tight.

faqs.q: How long does an underfloor heating installation take in Bonnyrigg?
faqs.a: For a typical ground-floor installation in a Bonnyrigg home, the physical installation takes two to four days. However, if a screed is poured, you'll need to allow three to four weeks for it to cure properly before laying finished floors. Older stone properties sometimes need additional prep time, so factor this into your renovation schedule from the start.

faqs.q: Do I need to do anything special because Bonnyrigg has moderately hard water?
faqs.a: Yes — your installer should fit a system inhibitor and a magnetic filter as standard. In a moderately hard water area like Bonnyrigg, limescale can gradually build up inside the manifold and pipework, reducing heat output and efficiency over time. These are inexpensive additions that protect the system. The filter should be checked and cleaned annually as part of routine servicing.

faqs.q: Can underfloor heating work with my existing boiler in Bonnyrigg?
faqs.a: It depends on the boiler's age and output. Underfloor heating runs best at lower flow temperatures than traditional radiator systems, which suits modern condensing boilers well. Older boilers common in Bonnyrigg's period properties may struggle to run efficiently at these lower temperatures. Your installer should carry out a compatibility check before the job starts — in some cases, a boiler upgrade alongside the UFH installation makes financial sense.
